# identity-public.txt — identity's public /v1 surface, as gateway enforces it.
#
# SOURCE: cafaye/identity, openapi/v1.yaml, every operation under /v1/* that
# declares `security: []`. Identity is the authority; gateway never invents an
# entry here. Do not hand-edit the list below: re-run the extraction and replace
# the whole body.
#
# Extracted 2026-10-15 from identity 9dc80c9, with:
#
#   python3 -c "
#   import re
#   lines = open('openapi/v1.yaml').read().splitlines()
#   cur_path = cur_op = cur_sec = None; ops = {}
#   def flush():
#       global cur_op, cur_sec
#       if cur_op and cur_path: ops.setdefault(cur_path, []).append((cur_op, cur_sec))
#       cur_op = None; cur_sec = 'auth'
#   for l in lines:
#       m = re.match(r'^  (/\S*):', l)
#       if m: flush(); cur_path = m.group(1); continue
#       m = re.match(r'^    (get|post|put|patch|delete|head|options):', l)
#       if m: flush(); cur_op = m.group(1).upper(); continue
#       m = re.match(r'^      security: \[\]', l)
#       if m and cur_op: cur_sec = 'public'
#   flush()
#   for p in sorted(ops):
#       for op, sec in ops[p]:
#           if p.startswith('/v1/') and sec == 'public': print(op, p)
#   "
#
# That run printed the 15 lines below — 15 operations on 15 paths (the brief's
# "seventeen" overcounts by two: the only other `security: []` hits in the file
# are identity's own /healthz and /readyz, which are not under /v1/*).
#
# FORMAT: one `METHOD /v1/path` per line. `{name}` is one template segment: it
# matches exactly one non-empty path segment, and the segment count must agree,
# so /v1/agents/claim/{token} opens /v1/agents/claim/abc and never /v1/agents
# itself, /v1/agents/claim, or /v1/agents/claim/abc/extra. The method is part
# of the entry: POST /v1/session is public and DELETE /v1/session is not.
